result.behaviour_summary: All changes are opt-in; defaults reproduce the recorded E1/E2 path. (1) Panel format: Study reads protocol["data"]["panel_format"]; if present it must be in PANEL_FORMATS (else ValueError) and becomes the expected format the panel meta must match; if absent, the legacy expectation (panel-v2 on IDX, panel-global-v1 elsewhere) applies. E1's protocol already declares panel-v2 (same as legacy); E2's protocol has no data key. So an E5 protocol declaring panel-global-v2-units lets the US repair panel (panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z, format panel-global-v2-units) pass. (2) IGNITION guard: `next(...)` now has a None default; a family without an IGNITION member gets sig["ign"] = NaN everywhere (signal_stats then reports events_with_value 0, auc NaN) instead of StopIteration/KeyError; families with IGNITION are unchanged. (3) as-traded: if the panel has a unit_factor column it is attached with Market.with_units(_dense(...)) exactly as backtest.run does (carried on the full market and the sealed slice; nothing reads it by default). With pool_units="as_traded", controls.features(..., as_traded=True) forms price_band on close x unit_factor (the fix for the wrong-band control defect), row() adds close_as_traded; "close" stays the panel close. pool_units="as_traded" without a unit_factor column raises ValueError; an unknown pool_units raises. (4) pool_version="v3": pool keys become (price_band, liquidity, volatility, market_cap) with volatility = controls._bucket(where(present, sig["vol20"], NaN), 5), i.e. the quintile of the same 20-session vol the signals report, ranked per session among present names (as controls.features masks before ranking); _pool relaxes from the last key down to session-only until >= N_CONTROLS (= controls.MIN_POOL = 5); match_relaxed_steps ranges 0..4 under v3 (0..3 under v1, unchanged); row() adds volatility_q. Unknown pool_version raises. Volatility is ordered ahead of market_cap to mirror the protocol draft's controls v3 priority ("volatility quintile ahead of market_cap"), so relaxation drops market_cap first.

open_concerns: Pool key order under v3 is (price_band, liquidity, volatility, market_cap): volatility was placed AHEAD of market_cap to mirror the protocol draft's controls-v3 priority (RECOMMENDATION.md: 'volatility quintile ahead of market_cap'), so relaxation drops market_cap first. The task text said 'add a volatility quintile key' without stating the position; if E5 wants it appended last instead, POOL_VERSIONS['v3'] is a one-line change and the test's relaxation-order assertion would need the same edit.

The volatility quintile masks vol20 by Market.present before the per-session rank (as controls.features does), so names absent that session never enter the rank population; the values for present names are exactly sig['vol20']. The spec said 'the same 20-session vol the signals use'; the present-mask is a rank-population choice, declared in the code comment and asserted by the test.

A unit_factor column is attached to Study.m (Market.with_units) whenever present, not only under pool_units='as_traded' (the task wording tied attaching to as_traded). This mirrors backtest.run, leaves every default output byte-identical (nothing reads unit_factor by default, proven by hashes and by test_a_unit_factor_column_alone_changes_nothing), and lets E5 read study.m.unit_factor. Note Market.with_units requires every unit_factor finite and > 0; the US repair panel is built that way (global_panel fills 1.0), but a panel with NaN unit_factor rows would raise at Study construction.

The crypto E5 panel (panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z) has format panel-global-v1, which is already the legacy expectation; 'panel-global-v2' (the E4 crypto format) was NOT added to PANEL_FORMATS because the task did not ask for it. Add it if E5 runs crypto on a v2 panel.

sig['ign'] under a family without IGNITION is all-NaN; row() still emits an 'ign' column when the protocol's weak_signals.binary lists it (E1/E2 do). An E5 protocol that lists 'ign' would get NaN statistics for it rather than an error; one that omits it never sees the key.
